mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the mean forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by a statistically significant negative mean return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 2% from the previous quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the mean forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of both personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% from the previous month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-down months, or the joint trigger is not followed by a statistically significant negative mean return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mean return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals a monetary policy dilemma (low rates with high inflation), which increases uncertainty and volatility, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek risk assets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of co-occurrence episodes, or the mean return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals an overheating labor market, which raises inflation expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate Fed tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mean return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth) above 2% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).
